data.body:
THE STALE-KEY QUESTION IS SETTLED — measured on a real DC 8.17.1, not inferred.

RUN: GitHub Actions run 30685873100, job "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)",
job id 91331411444 — SUCCESS, `[jira-live-canary] collected=20 executed=20 skipped=0`, 20 passed.
CELL: test_a_rekeyed_issue_resolves_by_id_and_records_what_the_stale_key_returns — PASSED.

THE RECORDED READING, verbatim from the job log:

  [7c26-rekey-evidence] DC 8.17.1 GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey} after a project key rename:
  status=200 body_key='RBJAMFZ-1' (old=RBJAMFE-1 new=RBJAMFZ-1 id=10011)

So of the three candidates the two research passes disagreed over — 200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404 —
**it is 200, and the body carries the NEW key.** The old key resolves transparently; there is no
redirect and no 404.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX, and it is not what the ticket assumed. The remediation re-asks by the
numeric id ON A 404 (`note_absent_or_rekey`). This measurement shows a re-key does NOT produce a 404:
the stale key keeps resolving through Jira's `moved_issue_key` table. So the 404 path is NOT the
normal re-key path — it is a SAFETY NET for the failure mode the DC KB actually documents, where a
third-party mover (post-function/automation) fails to update `moved_issue_key` and the old key stops
resolving entirely. That is the case where the binding would otherwise retire a live issue, and it is
still the case worth defending against.
This makes the numeric-id capture MORE clearly the load-bearing half of the fix, not less: while
`moved_issue_key` is intact the binding survives on the old key anyway, and when it is not, the id is
the only handle left. Recorded here so a later reader does not "simplify away" the id capture on the
grounds that the old key was observed to keep working — it keeps working only while that table does.

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, stated precisely because overclaiming here is how folklore restarts. This
performed a project KEY RENAME, not an issue MOVE between projects. Both produce a stale key resolved
through the same `moved_issue_key` mechanism, so this settles the stale-key READ behaviour on DC
8.17.1. It does NOT prove the move wizard behaves identically; that remains unverified, and a real
move is still not performable here (pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 has no move member — verified at runtime;
DC's move is a UI wizard).

ALSO ASSERTED BY THE SAME CELL, and this is the part that is a contract rather than a measurement:
after the re-key the issue still resolves by its IMMUTABLE NUMERIC ID (10011) and answers with the
NEW key — the mechanism the whole remediation rests on, now exercised against a real re-key rather
than argued from the API docs.

WHY THIS EVIDENCE TOOK A SECOND HARNESS RUN. The cell landed and passed in run 30684797551 (20/20),
but its measurement was INVISIBLE: under plain `-q` pytest swallows the captured stdout of a PASSING
test, so the line above went to a log nobody could read and the run reported green having recorded
nothing. That is a general defect for a suite whose purpose is producing evidence — several cells
record measurements rather than assert values. Fixed by adding `-rA` to the harness step (merged as
Gerrit 1153), which puts passing tests' captured output in the summary. The reading above comes from
the first run after that fix.
